newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes firmer as U.S. unit retreats.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes firmer as U.S. unit retreats.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed on a firm note on Tuesday, thanks to the weakness the U.S. unit and foreign funds buying.
The rate ended at T$27.482 versus T$27.491 at Monday's close. Turnover was an active US$241.5 million.

From a steady opening, the Taiwan dollar gained more ground in the first hour of trading. A late bout of Taiwan dollar buying pushed it to close at the day's peak. Some exporters had bet on quarter-end U.S. dollar demand from importers, which, however, failed to materialize. "There was some disappointed selling of U.S. dollars," said a foreign bank dealer.
In addition, dealers were reluctant to take long U.S. dollar positions before the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting set late on Tuesday Taiwan time.
"The market has priced in a small hike," the dealer said. "But few people have strong convictions about what the Fed might do."
If the Fed policy-makers decide to leave the Fed funds rate unchanged, the dollar could soften some more, she said.
Light foreign funds buying in a thin market towards the close gave the Taiwan dollar an additional boost, she said.
